title: Why retries wait longer each time
conclusion: Each retry waits twice as long as the last, so a struggling service gets room to recover.

sections.title: The retry ladder
sections.summary: Four tries, and the wait before each one doubles.
sections.what: A call that fails is tried again, but only after a pause, and every pause is twice the one before it.
sections.why: Doubling spreads the retries out, so many callers do not all hit a busy service at once.
sections.custom_explains: the four retry rungs and the doubling wait before each
sections.primary_visual: invented tide ladder: rungs on the left, rising waits on the right
sections.interaction: tick the box to outline the longest wait

custom_elements.explains: the four tries in the order they happen
the wait before each try, drawn as height

sections.title: Where the ladder stops
sections.summary: After the fourth try the call gives up and reports the failure.
sections.what: The fourth try is the last one; after it the caller stops and shows the error. This pattern is called backoff: the caller backs off a little more after every failure.

steps.title: Try 1
steps.body: The call fails; the caller waits 1 second.

steps.title: Try 2
steps.body: It fails again; the wait doubles to 2 seconds.

steps.title: Try 3
steps.body: Still failing; the caller waits 4 seconds.

steps.title: Try 4
steps.body: The last try. If it fails, the error is shown.

glossary.definition: waiting longer after each failed try before trying again
